10.4 Superficial Expansion

Under the application of heat, the area of a metallic plate increases. This phenomenon of expansion in area is referred to as the superficial expansion of the body. Thus, the change in the area of a body when subjected to heat is called the superficial expansion of the material. Superficial expansion can be observed by measuring the change in the area of a rectangular plate or the change in the area of a circular disc.

Suppose a metallic sheet of area A1 at temperature 1 is heated to temperature  so that its area becomes A2 due to thermal expansion as shown in figure 10.6. It is observed that the change in area (A2 – A1) is;
i. directly proportional to the original area A1 i.e. (A2 – A1)  A1
ii. directly proportional to the change in temperature i.e. (A2 – A1)  (2 – 1). . . (2)
Combining both equations (1) and (2), we get; (A2 – A1)  A1 (2 – 1)

If A1=1 unit of area and (2 – 1) = 1 unit of temperature then from equation (3),  = A2 – A1.
Therefore, the superficial expansivity  of a solid body is defined as the change in its area per unit original area per unit change in temperature. Its SI unit is K–1 .

10.5 Cubical Expansion

Under the application of heat, the volume of a solid body increases. This phenomenon of expansion in volume is referred to as the cubical expansion of the body. Thus, the change in volume of a body when subjected to heat is called the cubical expansion of the material. Cubical expansion can be observed by measuring the change in the volume of a solid sphere or the change in the volume of a cuboid.
